What changed: personas with profile pictures, in `media/personas`. `src/media/persona` draws adult personas (18 and over, `PERSONA_MIN_AGE`) from the warm-up's datasets (`drawPersona`: doomscrolling, social behaviour, DaRUS-3327). Each line of `personas.jsonl` holds the persona's characteristics, the rows it came from, the image prompt and avoid list, every generation attempt with SubQ's scores, and the picture's path. The prompt is built from the characteristics: the place from the occupation, the light from when they scroll, the mood. It follows the low-angle selfie style read from matt's two example photos, with no phone, screen or text words. The picture is generated through treg (`reapi.image-gen.gemini-3-pro-image`, 1K, 3:4) and saved as `<personaId>/profilePicture.png`. SubQ checks it against the persona: matchesPersona at least 0.7, and ageFits, genderFits, lifeFits, selfieStyle, looksReal, noText, armHidden, lowAngle and unflattering at least 0.6 each. Anything low is regenerated, and the prompt keeps a fix for every check that has failed so far. After 5 attempts the closest is kept with `matched: false`. armHidden (the arm holding the camera out of the picture or under 20% of it), lowAngle (the camera below the face pointing up at it) and unflattering came from matt's look at the first five, and the prompt asks for them from the first attempt. `--approve` locks the pictures matt likes: they are never rechecked or regenerated, and the first one becomes SubQ's third style example. `--redo <id>` rejects one picture and keeps its attempts on record. `--recheck` checks every picture that isn't approved and regenerates whichever fail. matt's example photos are only ever sent to SubQ as the style; they are never given to the image model, and never committed (`~/.logCli/personaExamples`). The skill is `personaPicture`. The naming check allows the external model id `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`.
Why: matt asked for a JSONL storing 5 random personas built from our data, each with their characteristics, kept in the same place as the listing media. He asked for a profile picture generated from each persona in the style of the two selfies he sent, stored in a subfolder per persona as profilePicture.png. SubQ checks whether each one matches its persona and regenerates it until it does, and the prompts are part of the JSONL that is fed to the image model via treg. Then he said an arm in the picture is bad and unnatural, that it must be an unflattering shot from below as a SubQ parameter, and that three of the five were perfect.
Checked: the first live run matched 5 of 5 with 13 images. The first draw picked a 14-year-old from the dataset and the treg body was mangled by the Windows shell; nothing was billed, and both were fixed (adults only, body sent as a file). matt rejected studentFemale25 and approved fullTimeEmployeeMale30, fullTimeEmployeeMale26 and freelancerSelfEmployedMale36. A recheck with the new checks failed studentMale30 on the arm (0.16) and the angle (0.25). He and studentFemale25 were regenerated and both matched on the first try. Altogether 21 images for 588 credits ($0.588). New tests cover the persona draw and prompt, adults only, the SubQ request, regenerating with the fixes building up until it matches, and keeping the closest when nothing matches.

What changed: the persona pictures no longer share a background. Each persona's place comes from its `profession` in the social behaviour dataset, or `Unemployed` from its occupation. There are three places per profession (`BACKGROUNDS`), and no two personas in a draw get the same one (`backgroundOf`). A second SubQ call shows each picture beside the other personas' pictures, three at a time, and asks whether its kind of room differs from every one of theirs (`backgroundDistinct`, `backgroundCheckRequest`). It asks about the kind of room only, because the first wording failed a classroom and a library for sharing ceiling tiles with an office. When that check fails, the persona moves to the next place for its profession before the retry (`nextBackground`, `backgroundsTried`). `--styleFrom <id>` makes one picture the style reference (freelancerSelfEmployedMale36, the one matt liked best). It is SubQ's fourth image, and `likeReference` asks whether the picture is taken the same way. The prompt now asks for that angle: a little below the face and off to one side, tilted, head turned. Images sent to SubQ are shrunk to 768 px JPEGs (`shrinkImage`), because four full-size PNGs passed SubQ's 8 MiB limit.
Why: matt said the pictures can't look the same: the backgrounds should be spun out from the profession and the dataset, and SubQ can take a few images to compare them. He said the freelancer one looks best and the two remade ones looked weird.
Checked: studentMale30 and studentFemale25 were redone live. Each went through 5 attempts without passing every check, so the closest was kept: a teacher in an empty classroom (every other check at least 0.94, backgroundDistinct 0.3 under the old wording) and a researcher between library shelves (every other check at least 0.8, backgroundDistinct 0.29). The two wrongly failed backgrounds are why the question was reworded; a home desk like the freelancer's rightly scored 0.03. The five pictures are now a classroom, an office, a library, a cubicle and a home desk. The approved three were not touched. Together with the earlier redos this came to 35 image generations, about $1. New tests cover distinct backgrounds within a draw, the background request, and swapping the background before a retry.

What changed: three X queue bugs fixed. (1) `log twitter queue plan --minGap`, `--limit`, `build --seed` and `nudge --replies` were ignored. The parser hands integer flags over as strings, and the queue only accepted a number, so `--minGap 600` planned 120 s apart. `wholeFlag` now reads them, and anything that isn't a whole number is refused. (2) A target can carry its own `text`, written for that person's post. `queue build` keeps it and draws only the other targets' lines from the variations, and `--variations` isn't needed when every target has its own. Two targets with the same text are refused. Before this, build shuffled every line across the targets, so personal lines had to be put back by hand. (3) A cancel stops a queue run during its waits and cool-offs, and before each send. `CommandContext.cancelled` comes from the MCP job (`jobCancel`). The run saves, says where it stopped, and resumes when run again. Before this, a cancel was only checked at a browser step, which a queue never has, so a cancelled run held the account until its next send.
Why: matt: "fix the bugs, don't turn it into an MCP tool", after the cold-caller run hit all three: `--minGap 600` planned 2 min apart, the 6 personal replies had to be matched to people by hand, and a cancelled run kept matthewsoldit busy through its 15-minute cool-off.
Checked: `bun test` over cli/twitter and mcp: 82 pass, 0 fail, with three new tests: minGap honoured and refused when not whole, own text kept with the rest drawn, a cancel stops a waiting run with nothing sent. `tsc --noEmit` clean. Live: `queue plan --window 75m --minGap 600` planned the 5 remaining cold-caller replies at least 600 s apart, and the run is sending them now.

What changed: X Chat (encrypted DMs) is read through log. X's own encryption SDK, chat-xdk v0.5.2, is vendored at `vendor/chatXdk` (Rust source plus its prebuilt Python wheel, installed from there). `vendor/twikit` reads keys and the Juicebox token map (`GetPublicKeysQuery`), unlocks with the PIN (`unlock_xchat`) and decrypts every conversation (`get_xchat_messages`), paging the X Chat inbox once per run. `log twitter chat pin` saves the PIN from a masked prompt after checking it against Juicebox. `log twitter dms` fills X Chat threads with their text, and `--with` merges a person's legacy and X Chat threads from one export read. New `log search` (MCP `search`, `searchIndex`, `searchBench`): BM25 (bm25s) plus meaning (verso-db HNSW over local all-MiniLM-L6-v2, embedded in a worker process so its sharp never meets the repo's) fused with RRF, filters by platform, account, person and day, indexes kept in ~/.logCli/search. Rules 88 and 89.
Why: matt: replies were going out from old legacy threads while the real conversations sat in encrypted X Chat ("DONT OPEN IT IN MY CHROME WE FUCKING BUILT IT OUT"), and finding context by reading every conversation is too slow; he asked for hybrid BM25 + vector search with RRF in Bun.
Checked: `bun run check` with LOG_PYTHON: 1102 pass, 0 fail, every gate green; twikit tests 3 pass. Live: the PIN unlocked through Juicebox; `log search index` read 200 conversations with X Chat decrypted (Zach's thread now shows "ty for sending! I dont think this is exactly what we need rn"); indexed 541 chunks in 24.4 s; `log search bench`: warm p50 3.81 ms, p95 5.55 ms, p99 8.39 ms (200 queries), cold p50 5.91 ms (first query 677 ms loading the model), linear scan 9.34 ms a query.

Live: the first sync wrote 610 articles to node02's Twenty and 3149 chunks to kb-redis in 268 s; a repeat sync wrote only the 2 new ones. Searches found the right article first or second ("why did the twenty tunnel go down", "messenger pin blocks the inbox" with `--kind pageState`, "where is the cloudflare api token", "launch budget opens per day"), and `kb remember` was searchable at once.

What changed: X's old DM thread (`<a>-<b>`) and its X Chat mirror (`<a>:<b>`) are one conversation everywhere (#59). New `src/twitter/dm/person`: `personKeyOf` gives both threads one key, `mergeThreads` makes them one row, `dropMirrors` shows a message mirrored into both once (same sender, same words with links ignored, within 5 s). `log twitter dms` lists one row per person with the newest message from either thread, and `--with` no longer shows a mirrored message twice. `log search index` merges each person's pair before chunking, so one hit, not two. The inbox watcher keys what it has seen per person, so one reply alerts once. The tool definitions carry it (`ONE_INBOX_NOTE`): `twitterDms` and `twitterDm` say the two threads are one inbox, a sent dm is delivered whichever id it names and is never resent, and a refusal before X (styleFailed, a dry run) sent nothing. A sent dm now says so in its answer.
Why: matt: "they're one, it might say they're two but they're one". An agent told him a reply had gone to "the other inbox" and he thought it was about to send twice; he asked for it in the tool definitions so every agent has it when it calls them.
Checked: `bun test src/twitter/dm src/search src/inbox`: 14 pass. `bun run check`: tsc clean, 1106 pass, 1 fail, `log reddit session check` > the engine runs on vendor/rdvwr, which fails the same on main without this change (run without LOG_PYTHON). Every lefthook gate green, docs rebuilt.

What changed: X Chat replies come by push, the way X's own chat app gets them (read with rea from X's shipped code, issue #68), instead of reading the whole inbox again and again. vendor/twikit: `generate_xchat_token` (GenerateXChatTokenMutation), `Client.watch_xchat` (one socket to wss://chat-ws.x.com/ws through the pinned curl_cffi session, a KeepAlive every 30 s, a fresh token and reconnect when it drops), `xchat.frame_of` (the Thrift binary Message union), and key priming so each pushed message decrypts (every conversation's key-change events once at start, the newest inbox page again for a key it doesn't have). Engine action `xchatWatch` prints one liveEvent line per message; `runTwitterEngineLive` streams them. New `log twitter chat watch --account <a> [--seconds] [--inbox] [--json]`. The inbox hook no longer polls: it keeps one `chat watch --inbox` per signed-in X account (pid file) and puts each new message in front of the agent with what to do: read the thread, draft from matt's guide, gate it, show matt, send only when he says. New `log voice --to --text [--context]` (src/twitter/copy/voice): SubQ reads a draft against GUIDES/MATT_WRITING_STYLE.md and dms matt wrote himself, and a phrase he never says fails it. Docs: docs/platforms/x/xchat/live.md (how it works, what was seen live, how to check it again when X changes), vendor/twikit/docs/xchat_live.md, skills/xchatReplies.
Why: matt: the polling kept hitting X's 429 (27 Oct 14:57 to 15:38, 28 Oct 03:2x and 05:15 UTC) and a 14-DM batch never went out; he asked for the notification system X's client uses, found with rea, built so the hooks act on what happens the way we did by hand (read, draft in his voice, SubQ gate, send), and written into vendored twikit so it's understood in future.
Checked: live on matthewsoldit, 28 Oct: the probe saw 40 messageEvent frames pushed in ~85 s; `log twitter chat watch --seconds 90` 8 messages pushed, nothing polled, exit 0; after key priming the 05:49:45 message opened live ('Ok wait let ai reply now'); the hook started the watchers and delivered each message with its steps; `log voice` gated three replies that were sent. `tests/test_xchat_frames.py` 6 pass, `src/twitter/copy/voice` 4 pass. `bun run check`: 1111 pass, 0 fail, every gate green, docs rebuilt.

What changed: Discord is log's next platform (`log new platform discord --noProxy`, like Reddit): its session, `log discord session check`, engine stub and docs, `DISCORD` added to Twenty's socialAccounts.platform (twentySetup keeps the 8 existing options), and the first account `sourcedandsoldtothehighestbidder` with its own AdsPower profile. `log inspect` now records WebSocket frames: `harRecorder.SocketTap` watches every page's sockets, inflates a `zlib-stream` socket with one context, redacts a token in the socket URL, and writes the frames into each step's network.har as `_webSocketMessages` on a 101 entry. `exchangesOf` turns each frame into a `socket` exchange named for its event (`RECV ws MESSAGE_CREATE`), in time order with the HTTP calls, and `fitBundle` folds repeated frames (first 3 of each kind) so SubQ can still read a step. The platforms diagram no longer breaks on a platform with no vendored client. docs/platforms/discord/README.md has what the inspect found: discord.gg is the invite domain (404 Unknown Invite), sign-in, Ctrl+K, history paging (`before` + `limit=20`), sending, and the gateway round trip with Jilly.
Why: matt: make Discord a new platform with no proxy, sign in step by step through log inspect, and since the reply came by push and the recording couldn't see it, fix inspect so it captures WebSocket frames, and roll every finding into the Discord platform's docs.
Checked: live on sourcedandsoldtothehighestbidder, 28 Oct: sign-in `POST /api/v9/auth/login` 200; scroll-up paging seen; two messages sent (log group chat, vibe coders #bot-help) and one to Jilly, whose reply came as `RECV ws MESSAGE_CREATE` 4.2 s after our POST, with TYPING_START, MESSAGE_REACTION_ADD and MESSAGE_ACK around it; step 02's reading went from 607222 tokens (SubQ 400) to 72311 after the fold, finding written and fixed. New tests: socketExchanges.test.ts 3 pass, python/browser/socketTapTest.py 4 pass. `bun run check`: 1117 pass, 0 fail, every gate green.

Discord signs in with a localStorage token, not a cookie, so a platform's shape can now name localStorage keys (`sessionStorage`): the gate looks for them in the row's `storageOrigins`, and the engine gets them beside the cookies (`storagePath`). A browser run on any platform but Facebook now saves its cookies and origins back to Twenty when it closes (`savePlatformSession`). DIRECT_ROUTES, the command's text, the README and diagrams say vendor/endcord. The Discord tests cover the token gate and the engine loading endcord.
Why: matt picked endcord from the client count (`clients.md`): vendor it and use it.
Checked: live: the account's browser opened and closed (11 cookies, 1 origin saved), then `log discord session check --account sourcedandsoldtothehighestbidder` answered loggedIn as sourcedandsoldtothehighestbidder from Discord's own answer, with no browser; a fake token answers 401 sessionDead. `bun run check`: 1118 pass, 0 fail, every gate green.

What changed: `log twitter dms` now syncs the inbox the way X's own chat app (dm-core) does. The first read takes the whole inbox once and keeps it in `~/.logCli/twitter/<account>/inboxSync.json` with the newest event's sequence id (`python/twitterApi/inboxSync.py`). Every read after asks only for what is newer: `GetMessageEventsPageQuery` from that sequence id (`client.get_xchat_updates` in vendor/twikit), beside one `dm/inbox_initial_state` for the old DMs, both at once. With nothing new there is no PIN unlock, no key fetch and no decrypt. When something is new it unlocks once and opens only those conversations' keys (`client.open_xchat_events`, `GetInboxPageConversationDataQuery`, up to 20 ids a call), keeping each event once by its id. The engine takes the user id from the twid cookie instead of two settings calls. Each read saves the conversations it changed (all of them on a full read) for `log search`, and starts `log search index --saved` in the background. That now runs `updateIndex`: only new or changed chunks are embedded (upserted), chunks that are gone are removed, and BM25 is rebuilt. `--rebuild` embeds everything again. The command says what it fetched (`synced in 1.27 s: 0 new X Chat events since sequence …`). `--full` reads everything again. The X→search mapper moved into the search library (`twitterConversationOf`). The test preload keeps conversations and the search index in temp folders. The X Chat doc records the bundle evidence, rea's partial reading and the timings.

The engine records the account's user id in the inbox store. `log twitter chat watch --inbox` writes each message X pushes into the store (`inboxSync.push_message`): kept once by id, with the sequence id left alone so the next sync still reads everything after it. The SessionStart hook adds who wrote last and is waiting, read from each X account's store with nothing fetched (`storedWaiting`, `storedInboxContext`). The hook's description and diagram say so.
Why: matt asked to cut the remaining start-up overhead: the hook should read the local inbox store with no network, and each dms read should make fewer Twenty lookups. Timed on 2026-10-30, the ~6 s outside the engine was Python imports 1.73 s, Bun loading every command 1.0 s, the account lookup 0.8 s, the PIN lookup 0.25 s, and a Twenty write on every read.
Checked: Python engine imports 1.73 s → 0.96 s (three runs). Live on matthewsoldit, six reads with nothing new, 10 s apart: whole command p50 4.6 s, max 6.5 s (was p50 6.4 s, max 9.1 s), engine p50 1.3 s, no Twenty write printed. Bun loading every command (~1 s) is unchanged.

Its instructions are short (1,567 characters, was 13,278, so the client no longer cuts them off): what log is, "You MUST load the full guide before other log tools: getGuide({ topic: "logMcpInstructions" })", and seven one-line hard rules. A new `getGuide` tool, listed first, serves `docs/guides/<topic>.md`, and its topic list names each guide. There are 14 guides (`GUIDE_TOPICS`, `src/mcp/server/helpers/guides.ts`), one per kind of work (facebookBrowser, facebookFlows, facebookMarketplace, facebookGroups, xInbox, xSending, xAccount, discord, reddit, accountsAndProxies, runsAndEvidence, knowledgeAndSearch, newPlatform), plus the core logMcpInstructions. The core guide carries rule one, all 25 core principles in full, which guide covers which work, and how runs report back. `bun run docs:build` writes every guide from the code: the work step by step (each topic's skills), every tool it covers with its full description and usage (`toolsFromCommands({ full: true })`), and every AGENTS.md rule those tools cite, in full. `check:docs` refuses a stale guide and a tool with no guide. Each tool's description is now short: what it does, its `log …` usage line, its notes, "Before first using this tool in a session, load its guide: getGuide({ topic: … })", then its rules. The engine paragraph naming the library behind a call (twikit, fbk, endcord, rdvwr) is gone from descriptions and guides, the usage text no longer names those libraries, and the hook's every-prompt "log-cli engines" block is now just each account's session and today's use.

And the libraries behind the engine (twikit and the like) give the agent no context, so they come out.

What changed: every tool the log MCP server lists, `getGuide` included, now carries `_meta: { "anthropic/maxResultSizeChars": 200000 }` (`RESULT_SIZE_META`, `src/mcp/server/types.ts`). This is Claude Code's documented way for a server to raise one tool's result limit. Without it, Claude Code saves any text result over 50,000 characters (or 25,000 tokens) to a file and gives the agent only the path. With it, results up to 200,000 characters arrive whole. The hard ceiling is 500,000.
Why: after the restart, matt had the agent call `getGuide({ topic: "logMcpInstructions" })` through the MCP only. The 72,209-character guide came back as "exceeds maximum allowed tokens … saved to <file>", so the agent never got the context the guides exist for. matt: don't hand-roll a fix, look it up in Claude Code's documentation. code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, "MCP output limits and warnings" and "Raise the limit for a specific tool", fetched through TinyFish on 2026-10-30. The Reddit thread matt sent is about a different limit, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, the 32,000-token cap on Claude's own reply.
Checked: a new test lists the tools over MCP and finds the limit on every one, 200,000 under the 500,000 ceiling. Every guide fits under it: the biggest, facebookFlows, is about 93K. MCP tests: 63 pass, tsc clean. The running log server needs reconnecting (/mcp) before it serves the new list.

What changed: X Chat messages that showed as "(could not decrypt)" open. Four causes, each read from chat-xdk's own answer. (1) A catch-up read brought messages without the key changes that open them: chat-xdk's error names the version needed, and `_xchat_decrypt` now asks `GetConversationPageQuery` for that conversation's `missing_conversation_key_change_events`, as X's app does, and decrypts again (`_xchat_missing_keys`, `_xchat_fetch_key_changes`). (2) chat-xdk drops a key change whose signer's signature it can't verify (`enforce_ckey_signatures`), and in a group the signer isn't always a current participant: every event's sender is now in the public-key lookup. (3) Reactions, edits, photos, shared posts and read markers decrypted fine but only `content.text` was read: `message_of` reads chat-xdk's `content_type` (`(reacted 🔥)`, `(edited) …`, `(image: name.jpg)`, the post's URL) and read markers are hidden everywhere (`is_marker`, `inboxSync.shown`), never counted as a chat's last message. (4) `--conversation g…` went to the old DM path: `is_xchat_id`. Messages held from before are opened again when their chat is read (`reopen`, up to 5) and by each inbox sync (`reopen_unopened`, 3 conversations a sync, once a day each), and the sync line says how many. The older-page read takes the key version from chat-xdk when the Thrift doesn't give it (`_xchat_versions`), and `--with` writes what it opened back into the store. Written up in `docs/platforms/x/xchat/README.md`.
Why: matt: the "could not decrypt" messages (Shaw's first line, Jash's latest, RVA's replies, the group chat) can't be an issue, since we go through X's own client: find the cause and fix it.
Checked: live on matthewsoldit, each read once: RVA 25 of 25 open (his three replies this morning, both photos, two reactions), Jash 7 of 7 (his 'could not decrypt' was an edit), the group 141 of 142 (the one left is from 12 July, under a key older than the oldest page X answers), Shaw's 21:30:01 now opens. twikit X Chat tests 12 pass (4 new: every content type, the missing key read from the error, the key changes fetched then opened again with the signers' keys, a held message reopened). Inbox sync tests 7 pass (new: a read marker is never the last message, group ids route to X Chat).
